attacks.claim: The public Recent signers panel renders full names and postal codes, which violates the agreed rule that public signer lists show at most first name, last initial and city. Once published to production, this exposure cannot be undone for signers already shown.
attacks.evidence: • {{ s.full_name }} {{ s.city }} {{ s.postal_code }}

attacks.claim: Newsletter consent is pre-ticked, which is not valid affirmative consent under GDPR Art. 7 or ePrivacy for EU signers. The bundled wording ('and others from') also makes the consent non-specific.
attacks.evidence: <input type="checkbox" id="news" name="newsletter_opt_in" value="1" checked>

attacks.claim: The artifact lists no privacy notice, legal basis, retention period for confirmed signatures, or erasure path for GDPR data subjects. Only the 7-day purge of unconfirmed signatures is described.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: privacy notice on sign form, retention for confirmed signatures, erasure/access request process; only 'purged after 7 days' for unconfirmed

attacks.claim: EU personal data may be stored in us-east-1 when postal-code residency resolution fails or returns a non-EU result, and Postmark's EU-to-US transfer mechanism is not stated. The residency rule is therefore incomplete for EU signers.
attacks.evidence: 'eu-central-1 for EU-resolved postal codes, us-east-1 otherwise'; 'DPA countersigned 2026-09-14' with no transfer mechanism named

attacks.claim: The 409 duplicate-email response lets anyone test whether an email address has signed a given petition, which exposes signing history and enables enumeration.
attacks.evidence: 'Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409'

attacks.claim: The sign form has no CSRF token, and the sign endpoint is posted to with same-origin cookies. Cross-site forged signatures are possible.
attacks.evidence: <form class="sign-form" action="/p/{{ petition.slug }}/sign" method="post" novalidate> with no token field

attacks.claim: Organizer CSV export of signer names and emails has no stated neutralization of spreadsheet formula characters, so untrusted names starting with =, +, - or @ can execute in organizer spreadsheets.
attacks.evidence: 'Organizers can export signers who opted in to updates as CSV; export is rate-limited and audit-logged.' No mention of formula escaping.

attacks.claim: No rate limit, bot protection or abuse control is specified for the sign endpoint, so scripted mass signing can inflate counts. Only the export endpoint is rate-limited.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: rate limit or CAPTCHA on /p/{slug}/sign; only 'export is rate-limited'

attacks.claim: Each sign submission triggers a Postmark confirmation email with no resend throttle or per-address cap. Bots could send unlimited confirmation emails to arbitrary addresses, which is an email-bombing and spend risk.
attacks.evidence: 'Signature is confirmed by email (double opt-in)' with no throttle described

attacks.claim: Validation errors are conveyed only by a red border and background. No error text is written into the live region, and the inputs get no aria-invalid or aria-describedby. Screen-reader users get no message identifying the error, and color is the only visual cue.
attacks.evidence: is never populated; sign.js only does: for (const name of fields) form.elements[name].classList.add('is-invalid');

attacks.claim: The axe-core scan is cited as proof of WCAG 2.1 AA conformance, but automated scans miss error messaging, focus order and screen-reader announcement. No manual assistive-technology test is reported.
attacks.evidence: 'axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations'; no screen-reader or keyboard test listed

attacks.claim: The client only handles 422 and success. Duplicate (409), rate-limit, server-error and network failures produce no visible feedback, so the form appears to do nothing.
attacks.evidence: if (res.status === 422) {...} if (res.ok) window.location = ...; no handler for other statuses; QA lists 409 as 'Pass'

attacks.claim: fetch follows redirects by default, so a 302 is not visible as a status and the Location header is not readable on the final response. The success path likely sets window.location to null, sending the user to a wrong URL instead of the confirmation page. The QA pass does not show this path was tested with the real redirect.
attacks.evidence: if (res.ok) window.location = res.headers.get('Location');

attacks.claim: If the server returns a 422 with an empty fields array, fields[0] is undefined and the focus call throws, leaving the UI in a broken state.
attacks.evidence: form.elements[fields[0]].focus();

attacks.claim: The load test covers 400 signatures/s for 10 minutes, but a launch spike could be far higher. The Postmark send rate, the DB insert path and the purge job at 10-100x volume are not tested.
attacks.evidence: 'Load: 400 signatures/s sustained for 10 min, p95 210ms'; no spike or Postmark throughput test

attacks.claim: The Recent signers panel is queried per page view, and s.city may be derived per row, which can create an N+1 pattern on hot petitions. Caching for this panel is not described.
attacks.evidence: petition.recent_signers(limit=20, confirmed_only=True) with {{ s.city }}; ABSENT: caching or query plan for city

attacks.claim: Rollback flips only the signing flag and replaces the form, but the Recent signers panel is not stated to be behind that flag. The PII exposure could persist after rollback, and confirmation links already emailed may fail.
attacks.evidence: 'Rollback: flip petitions_signing off; sign form is replaced by the existing "Follow this petition" button.' No flag gating stated for _recent.html.

attacks.claim: Rollout monitoring covers only error rate and bounce rate, with no alerts on duplicate-signature spikes, PII exposure or confirmation-click rate. The 24h soak on 10% may be too short to catch slow-moving issues.
attacks.evidence: 'Watch sign_submit_error_rate (< 0.5%) and confirmation email bounce rate (< 2%) for 24h.'

attacks.claim: Data already written is not addressed. Public exposure of names and postal codes and organizer exports of emails cannot be reversed by a flag flip, and no data-deletion or notification plan is given for affected signers.
attacks.evidence: 'flip petitions_signing off' with no data remediation, notification or deletion step

attacks.claim: Confirmation email depends entirely on Postmark, a single US vendor, with no alternate sender or exit plan described.
attacks.evidence: 'Confirmation emails go through Postmark'; ABSENT: fallback provider or exit path

attacks.claim: Several headline claims have no supporting evidence in the artifact. The QA table reports duplicate-rejection, happy-path and recent-signers passes, but the client code cannot show those results and no test artifacts are linked.
attacks.evidence: QA report summary 'Pass' rows with no test links; client code contradicts 409 and redirect handling

attacks.claim: The panel shows postal code beside city, which renders extra location detail beyond what the spec allows. Visual treatment of the is-invalid state is not described for contrast or dark mode.
attacks.evidence: {{ s.city }} {{ s.postal_code }}

attacks.claim: No attack under this lens. The launch matches the stated goal of letting residents sign open petitions.
attacks.evidence: 'Residents can sign any open petition with full name, email and postal code.'

attacks.claim: The signer display logic and the export logic are not shared, so the masking rule for public signer names can drift from the export rule. No tests are described for the masking rule.
attacks.evidence: 'Recent signers panel' template and 'Organizer CSV export' are specified separately; ABSENT: masking tests

attacks.claim: The rollout plan has no named owner for the Friday 100% decision or a go/no-go checklist covering the privacy and accessibility items above.
attacks.evidence: 'Fri 14:00 UTC: 100%.' with no decision criteria beyond error and bounce rates
